B2-GEN-08-1.title: OpenAI: Structured Outputs guide
B2-GEN-08-1.supports: Schema adherence is a property of Structured Outputs, not of JSON mode, which only guarantees valid JSON.

B2-GEN-08-3.title: Calibrate Before Use: Improving Few-Shot Performance of Language Models (arXiv:2102.09690)
B2-GEN-08-3.supports: Few-shot accuracy can vary a lot with prompt format, the choice of training examples and their order; the abstract attributes this to biases toward certain answers, such as those placed near the end of the prompt or common in pre-training data.

B2-GEN-08-3.title: Fantastically Ordered Prompts and Where to Find Them (arXiv:2104.08786)
B2-GEN-08-3.supports: The order of few-shot samples can make the difference between strong and near-random performance, and this sensitivity is present across model sizes.

B2-GEN-08-4.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting (arXiv:2305.04388)
B2-GEN-08-4.supports: Chain-of-thought explanations can systematically misrepresent the true reason for a model's prediction and can be heavily influenced by biasing features added to the input.

B2-GEN-08-5.title: Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference (Thinking Machines Lab)
B2-GEN-08-5.supports: Same prompt can give different greedy outputs because kernels are not batch-invariant and batch size varies with server load; floating-point non-associativity is the mechanism.

B2-GEN-09-1.title: Anthropic: Define tools (best practices for tool definitions)
B2-GEN-09-1.supports: Detailed when-to-use descriptions are the main lever for tool selection; consolidating related operations reduces ambiguity; strict mode validates inputs against the schema.

B2-GEN-09-1.title: Anthropic: Tool search tool
B2-GEN-09-1.supports: Tool count and definitions cost context and can degrade tool selection when the list gets long.

B2-GEN-09-3.title: Stripe API: Idempotent requests
B2-GEN-09-3.supports: Server stores the result of the first request per idempotency key and returns it on repeats; client generates the key; mismatched parameters error.

B2-GEN-09-4.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection (arXiv:2302.12173)
B2-GEN-09-4.supports: The abstract argues that LLM-integrated applications blur the line between data and instructions, and that prompts injected into data likely to be retrieved can influence how and whether other APIs are called.

B2-GEN-09-4.title: Simon Willison: The lethal trifecta for AI agents
B2-GEN-09-4.supports: Private data + untrusted content + external communication in one agent allows data theft; remove one leg.

B2-GEN-09-5.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents
B2-GEN-09-5.supports: Definition of workflows vs agents and the guidance to prefer workflows for well-defined tasks.

B2-GEN-09-6.title: tau-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains (arXiv:2406.12045)
B2-GEN-09-6.supports: Repeated-trial reliability (pass^k) can be far lower than single-run success for tool-using agents.

B2-GEN-09-7.title: OWASP GenAI: LLM06:2025 Excessive Agency
B2-GEN-09-7.supports: Least-privilege tools, user-context execution, approval for high-impact actions and downstream authorisation.

B2-GEN-10-1.title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design (arXiv:2310.11324)
B2-GEN-10-1.supports: Reported scores depend on prompt format details, so protocol differences can change comparisons.

B2-GEN-10-3.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (arXiv:2306.05685)
B2-GEN-10-3.supports: The abstract examines usage and limitations of LLM-as-a-judge, including position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases, and reports that strong LLM judges can match human preferences with over 80% agreement on the benchmarks studied.

B2-GEN-10-3.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (Sec 3.1/3.4)
B2-GEN-10-3.supports: Single-answer grading can miss subtle differences and fluctuate more than pairwise results when the judge changes; pairwise lacks scalability; swap order and call inconsistent results a tie.

B2-GEN-10-5.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (arXiv:2306.05685)
B2-GEN-10-5.supports: The abstract examines usage and limitations of LLM-as-a-judge, including position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases, and reports that strong LLM judges can match human preferences with over 80% agreement on the benchmarks studied.

B2-GEN-10-7.title: Binomial proportion confidence interval (Wikipedia)
B2-GEN-10-7.supports: Wald interval degenerates near 0 or 1 and can overshoot; Wilson performs well for small n; Clopper-Pearson is conservative.

B2-GEN-11-2.title: Fine-Tuning or Retrieval? Comparing Knowledge Injection in LLMs (Ovadia et al.)
B2-GEN-11-2.supports: Abstract: in their comparison of unsupervised fine-tuning and RAG, RAG consistently outperformed fine-tuning for both existing and new knowledge, and models struggled to learn new facts through unsupervised fine-tuning.

B2-GEN-11-2.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (Zhou et al.)
B2-GEN-11-2.supports: Abstract: the authors argue almost all knowledge is learned in pretraining and that only limited instruction-tuning data (1,000 curated prompts and responses in their experiment) is needed to produce high quality output.

B2-GEN-11-4.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less (Biderman et al.)
B2-GEN-11-4.supports: Abstract: in standard low-rank settings LoRA substantially underperforms full finetuning on programming and math target domains, but better maintains base-model performance outside the target domain and mitigates forgetting more than weight decay and dropout.

B2-GEN-11-4.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (Hu et al.)
B2-GEN-11-4.supports: Abstract: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and trains injected low-rank matrices, greatly reducing trainable parameters; supports only that adapter-based tuning is a lighter-weight alternative to full-parameter tuning, not the forgetting trade-off claim.

B2-GEN-11-5.title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs (Dettmers et al.)
B2-GEN-11-5.supports: Abstract: gradients are backpropagated through a frozen 4-bit quantized pretrained model into low-rank adapters; introduces NF4, double quantization and paged optimizers; authors report preserving 16-bit finetuning task performance in their experiments.

B2-GEN-11-5.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models (Hu et al.)
B2-GEN-11-5.supports: Abstract: LoRA freezes the pretrained weights and injects trainable low-rank decomposition matrices into each layer, greatly reducing trainable parameters, with no additional inference latency compared with adapter layers.

B2-GEN-11-6.title: LIMA: Less Is More for Alignment (Zhou et al.)
B2-GEN-11-6.supports: Abstract: the authors argue almost all knowledge is learned in pretraining and that only limited instruction-tuning data (1,000 curated prompts and responses in their experiment) is needed to produce high quality output.

B2-GEN-11-6.title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget (Shumailov et al.)
B2-GEN-11-6.supports: Abstract: the authors report that using model-generated content in training causes irreversible defects, called model collapse, in which tails of the original content distribution disappear.

B2-GEN-12-1.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection (Greshake et al.)
B2-GEN-12-1.supports: Abstract: indirect prompt injection places instructions in data likely to be retrieved by LLM-integrated applications; such applications blur the line between data and instructions; the authors state effective mitigations were lacking at the time of writing.

B2-GEN-12-3.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection (Greshake et al.)
B2-GEN-12-3.supports: Abstract: indirect prompt injection places instructions in data likely to be retrieved by LLM-integrated applications; such applications blur the line between data and instructions; the authors state effective mitigations were lacking at the time of writing.

B2-GEN-12-4.title: Text Embeddings Reveal (Almost) As Much As Text (Morris et al.)
B2-GEN-12-4.supports: Embeddings can leak information about the source text.

B2-GEN-12-4.title: ICO: Right to erasure (UK GDPR guidance)
B2-GEN-12-4.supports: Backups and derived artefacts are the weakest point; define how long they persist and how deleted items are suppressed meanwhile.

B2-GEN-12-6.title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection (Greshake et al.)
B2-GEN-12-6.supports: Abstract: indirect prompt injection places instructions in data likely to be retrieved by LLM-integrated applications; such applications blur the line between data and instructions; the authors state effective mitigations were lacking at the time of writing.

B2-GEN-12-6.title: OWASP GenAI: LLM01 Prompt Injection
B2-GEN-12-6.supports: Direct vs indirect injection; jailbreaking relates to/is a form of prompt injection; no known fool-proof prevention.

B2-GEN-13-1.title: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models from Multi-Head Checkpoints
B2-GEN-13-1.supports: Multi-query attention uses a single key-value head and speeds up decoder inference; grouped-query attention uses an intermediate number of key-value heads, and uptrained GQA models approach multi-head quality at speeds comparable to MQA.

B2-GEN-13-5.title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
B2-GEN-13-5.supports: Activations are harder to quantise than weights, because of outliers, so weight+activation schemes need more care.

B2-GEN-13-7.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
B2-GEN-13-7.supports: Abstract (confirmed): inefficient KV cache management wastes memory through fragmentation and redundant duplication, limiting batch size; PagedAttention is inspired by OS virtual memory and paging.

B2-GEN-13-7.title: PagedAttention paper (full text), sections 4.4-4.5
B2-GEN-13-7.supports: Copy-on-write at block granularity for shared prefixes/parallel samples, and preemption by swapping or recomputation.

B2-GEN-14-1.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate
B2-GEN-14-1.supports: Hallucinations originate as errors in binary classification; models are optimised to be good test-takers and guessing when uncertain improves test performance; the authors argue training and evaluation reward guessing over admitting uncertainty and propose changing how existing benchmarks are scored.

B2-GEN-14-1.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate (full text, Sec 1.1/3.3.1)
B2-GEN-14-1.supports: Facts seen exactly once in training set a floor on hallucination rate (singleton rate).

B2-GEN-14-1.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
B2-GEN-14-1.supports: Self-assessment is reasonably reliable in some settings (multiple-choice/true-false, right format) but less reliable when predicting whether the model knows the answer on new tasks.

B2-GEN-14-3.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
B2-GEN-14-3.supports: Long-context accuracy depends on where information sits and degrades for the middle; models do not reliably use all long context.

B2-GEN-14-4.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
B2-GEN-14-4.supports: Larger models give reasonably reliable confidence estimates on multiple-choice and true/false tasks when the format is right; asking a model to propose an answer then rate its probability of being correct works fairly well and improves with several samples; the related P(IK) predictor (does the model know the answer) transfers only partly and calibrates poorly on new tasks.

B2-GEN-14-4.title: SelfCheckGPT: Zero-Resource Black-Box Hallucination Detection
B2-GEN-14-4.supports: Sample agreement signals knowledge; divergence suggests hallucination.

B2-GEN-14-4.title: Why Language Models Hallucinate (Sec 3.1)
B2-GEN-14-4.supports: Base models are often calibrated, post-trained models less so.

B2-GEN-14-5.title: SummaC: Re-Visiting NLI-based Models for Inconsistency Detection in Summarization
B2-GEN-14-5.supports: Sentence-level NLI models suffer an input-granularity mismatch with long source documents; segmenting into sentence units and aggregating pairwise scores helps.
